verdict.reasoning: Patient reports right knee pain and clicking with reduced running tolerance and intermittent toe tingling: "my knees are hurting, and they're clicking a lot... I can't run very far... sometimes I also get this weird tingling in my toes" and later clarifies it's the right knee and right toes.
Onset: "So probably, it's been about two weeks."

Marathon training and distance: "I'm currently training for a marathon... maybe like seven or eight miles... I've done like, you know, four or five miles, and I've just done like a couple of seven, mile runs." Timing of pain: "probably starts off like after, uh, maybe, twenty minutes or so... somewhere around mile, three maybe, two and a half or three miles."
"the last time I actually stopped, I mean I ran a little bit longer, but then I stopped, because it was um... I feel like it's getting worse."

Location: "it's actually my right knee that hurts" and "I feel it, it's kind of weird, I feel it in the middle, but I almost feel like maybe it kind of uh, um, moves to the right, to the right of my knee a little bit."
Clicking with flex‑extend during abs: "when I start doing my abs... to kind of go from the flex position on my knees, and straighten my legs, then I feel all this clicking."

Mild swelling after first run and resolved with ice: "the first time I ran, it was a little bit swollen, but then I just put some like ice on it, and it went away." No pain at rest: "right now it's not swollen, and right now it doesn't hurt, you know."
No giving way or locking, stairs/walking okay: she denies giving way (describes only pain), "No" to locking when standing, "No" to problems on stairs, and "No, none" to problems walking.
Full ROM: Doctor asks, "Are you able to fully straighten the leg?... And what about fully flex it?" Patient: "Yes... Yes."
"there was this tingling in my toes... after the run... on my right toes" and later: "No it was just, it was that time."
Denials: Doctor: "Any change in colour, or temperature of your lower legs?" Patient: "No." Also: "any pain in the back of the calf" Patient: "No, no, nothing like that, no."
Other joints: Doctor asks about other joint problems and swelling; patient: "No." Then only notes transient sock indentation without persistent swelling.
"I play some ice hockey, and I had this injury a few months ago... I just like, fell on the ice and... had a, huge bruise."
"I mean I, I do have, I'm far-sighted."
"I'm far-sighted, and so I had uh, I had Lasik surgery."
"once I had this really bad UTI, they thought it was kidney stones, and so they had me actually in ER."
"I take Ibuprofen... nothing like major maybe, like, four hundred milligrams max."
"Sometimes, you know, just for cramps, I'll take... ibuprofen, or actually, uh, I'll take, what am I taking? Aleve." Aleve is naproxen.
"Well, I'll take uh, I take vitamin D."
"I take melatonin."
"occasionally, if I'm really having hard times... sleeping, I'll take Xanax."
"I'm currently training for a marathon" and describes frequent running and gym workouts, indicating high activity level.
"I also sometimes will um, you know, smoke a joint." (cannabis).

Right knee pain with activity and clicking in a runner is directly stated. The doctor notes need for exam for structural issues: "Ultimately we probably need to, examine the knee" and may need imaging "to... see if there's any problem with the, cartilage," so internal derangement not excluded is a reasonable direct clinical inference.
"there was this tingling in my toes... after the run... on my right toes" and later: "No it was just, it was that time."
"definitely carrying on with the ice therapy that you've been using. So, as much as you can, 'cause that really does make a difference."
"I would, try and ease up on the running, if you can. And if it's painful enough that you're, having to stop running, then it's not a good idea, to do that."
"I can prescribe you a slightly stronger, anti-inflammatory that you can take regularly instead of the Ibuprofen... But make sure that with food."
"I can prescribe you a slightly stronger, anti-inflammatory... but not with the Ibuprofen."
"the best thing I would, suggest, getting a appointment with the physiotherapist first, who can do like a long, assessment, and examination of the knee."
"then we can make an assessment as to whether we need to do any, um, imagery to, have a look inside the knee, and see if there's any problem with the, cartilage."

"If in the meantime you develop like persistant swelling, heat, redness, um, of the knee, or high temperature, feel unwell, or it completely locks up and you can't bend and stretch it... Then, you'd need to see a doctor urgently."
Prescription: "I'll send it through to your pharmacy for you." Referral/clinic: earlier, "we can, we can do a referral" to physio and "we can see you in our clinic as well" if wait is long.

"right now it's not swollen, and right now it doesn't hurt"; full ROM: "Are you able to fully straighten... fully flex..." "Yes... Yes."; and "Any problems going up and down stairs? Patient: No." "Any problems just walking normally? Patient: No, none."
